messages:
mia: kicking off a config-only deploy for routing/batching limits (staggered tenant floor adjustments + timeout tighten). change window 10:30-10:45 PT. will pin variants for critical tenants first. link to release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/rc-2026-03-21

leo: thanks — which params exactly?

mia: set of changes: 
- routing.weight_floor default 0.02 -> 0.04
- tiny_batch.max_tokens 32 -> 24
- per_request.timeout_ms 15000 -> 12000
- prefer_local_region:true for EU tenants
(everything is config-only, no model binary changes)

sam: can we stage by tenant cohort? prefer rolling unaffected -> low-risk tenants first then critical.

mia: yes. plan: cohort A (dev+internal) 10:30, cohort B (low-traffic) 10:34, cohort C (critical paid) 10:38 with a 2m observation per cohort. manual hold if latency or 5xx spike.

ops-kai: deploy-bot please queue and annotate canary. ops on standby.

deploy-bot: [deploybot] queued config update rc-2026-03-21 to env:prod. canary cohort A scheduled at 1712350001. rollback window passive until 1712350201. Notify with /deploy abort to cancel.

ana: typo — we agreed prefer_local_region only for EU tenant tag, not all EU traffic. confirm filter in rollout?

mia: good catch. rollout filter: tenant.tags contains "eu-regional". I'll update the rollout config snippet before canary.

leo: observability checks? set of alerts to watch: 95p latency, 5xx rate, kvcache hitrate. threshold: +20% latency, +0.5% 5xx.

sam: also watch batching queues: if avg batch size drops >30% that could hurt throughput, revert.

ops-kai: added temporary dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/routing/rc-2026-03-21

deploy-bot: canary cohort A started. applying config to 1% of traffic (dev tenants).

mia: monitoring first cohort, ping me on any >5xx or latency drift.

leo: seeing slight latency drop (good). no 5xx. batch size down 10% but within expectations. :thumbsup:

sam: rolling to cohort B now?

deploy-bot: cohort A healthy -> promoting cohort B at 10:34 PT. applying to 10% traffic.

ops-kai: added short-circuit rollback playbook in case of tenant-specific errors: 
- run /deploy abort to stop rollout
- pin routing config back to rc-2026-03-14
- escalate to eng-runtime if >1% persistent 5xx in any tenant for 3m

mia: note: for critical paid tenants we're doing manual pinning: we will pin to previous routing weight for tenants marked "paid-critical" rather than full rollout if anything odd.

deploy-bot: cohort B complete, no regressions detected. initiating cohort C manual approval step.

mia: taking manual approval — double-checking EU filter and timeouts. approving. starting cohort C at 10:38 PT to 30% then ramp to 100% over 7m if stable.

leo: quick reminder in release notes: this change tightens timeouts which can surface latent errors in integrations, advise support to watch tenant logs.

sam: adding note to support playbook and ticket template.

ops-kai: cohort C rolling. watchlist created for top 20 paid tenants.

deploy-bot: cohort C at 30% - monitoring. automated canary metrics stable.

mia: two minutes into cohort C — seeing one tenant with 502 bursts (tenant id t-984).

ops-kai: isolating t-984: bumping pin for that tenant back to previous weight_floor, will route them to fallback pool.

deploy-bot: manual pin applied for tenant t-984 -> pinned to rc-2026-03-14 config. traffic split updated.

mia: good. check if errors persist for that tenant after pin.

leo: errors subsided after pin. batch size and latency for t-984 restored.

sam: decision: continue rollout for other tenants, keep t-984 pinned and follow up postmortem. mark rollout as partial with tenant isolation.

mia: agreed. finalizing release notes with tenant isolation recorded. scheduling follow-up: postmortem + integration test against tightened timeout for t-984 next week.

deploy-bot: rollout finished: 97% of tenants updated, 1% pinned (t-984), 2% staged (paused per manual hold). please file any follow-ups in #postmortems referencing 1712350001.

mia: thanks team — ops offhand for 30m. I'll update the changelog and send brief to support. :slightly_smiling_face:
